deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a footnote, in H. Weber's hand, copied from Riemann's drafts for 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857). It belongs to the part of that paper (§§26-27) where theta quotients define functions f on the surface s,z that are not single-valued. On crossing the cuts (Querschnitte) a_ν, b_ν such an f picks up constant factors exp(2πi h_ν) and exp(2πi g_ν), with h_ν and g_ν rational. f has p simple poles at points (σ_μ, ς_μ), μ = 1..p, and depends on them algebraically.

(1) Let n be the least common denominator of all h_ν and g_ν. Then each factor raised to the n-th power is 1. Hence F = f^n is single-valued on the surface, i.e. a rational function R(s,z). [Mine:] f^n is likewise single-valued in each pair (σ_μ, ς_μ). So f is the n-th root of a rational function.

(2) Conditions on R = f^n:
- R has poles of exact order n at the p points (σ_μ, ς_μ).
- R therefore has np zeros counted with multiplicity (a rational function has as many zeros as poles).
- Since f itself is meromorphic locally, these np zeros must coincide in n-fold groups.
- Modern form: div R = n(D' − D), with D = Σ(σ_μ, ς_μ) and D' an effective divisor of degree p. Equivalently, D' − D is an n-torsion class in the Jacobian. Through Abel's theorem it corresponds to the theta characteristic (g, h).

(3) Second remark. Let t(s,z) be any function with the same factors at the cuts as f. Put d_μ = t(σ_μ, ς_μ).
- Then f/t has trivial factors in (s,z), so it is rational in (s,z).
- [Mine, implicit:] In Riemann's theta representation f depends on the arguments through u(x) − Σ u(σ_μ). So as a function of each (σ_μ, ς_μ), f has the inverse factors. These are compensated by the factor d_μ, which carries the factors of t.
- Hence ρ = f · t^{-1} · d_1 d_2 … d_p is single-valued, and thus rational, in (s,z) and in all pairs (σ,ς).
- Therefore f = ρ t / (d_1 d_2 … d_p).

This separates f into:
- a fixed multiplicative (Prym-type) function t carrying the monodromy;
- a rational function ρ;
- a normalization in the parameters σ.

The closing bracket states the provenance: a remark from the drafts in Riemann's Nachlass for the preceding paper. The pencil note 'Handschrift von H. Weber' identifies the writer. The remark appears (essentially verbatim) as a footnote in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke.
errors: The claim that f · t^{-1} · d_1…d_p is rational in the (σ,ς) is stated without proof. It relies on f having multipliers in each (σ_μ, ς_μ) inverse to its multipliers in (s,z); this is true for Riemann's theta-quotient representation but is not argued on the page.
'unendlich von der nten Ordnung' at each of the p points presupposes the (σ,ς) are distinct and f has simple poles there (general position).

results.what: An algebraic function with rational characteristic multipliers at the cuts is the n-th root of a rational function R (n = common denominator), with div R = n(D' − D), deg D = p.
results.modern_name: Root functions (Wurzelfunktionen) / n-torsion line bundles; n-torsion points of the Jacobian and theta characteristics of order n
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (Abelsche Functionen); developed by Weber, Prym, Klein, Schottky, Frobenius

results.what: Representation f = ρ t / (d_1…d_p), with t any function having the same multipliers and ρ rational in (s,z) and the (σ,ς).
results.modern_name: Sections of a flat line bundle differ by meromorphic functions; normalization of Prym (multiplicative) functions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Werke footnote); Prym functions systematized by Prym and Rost / Appell

deep.surprise_reason: A Weber copy of a Riemann draft remark that was printed as a footnote in Riemann's Werke. The content is standard for the theory of root functions and theta characteristics, so nothing new is attributed.

checkable.sympy: a1,a2,a3,a4,t=symbols('a1 a2 a3 a4 t'); R=(z-a1)/(z-a2); series(R.subs(z,a2+t**2)*t**2, t, 0, 1)
checkable.asserts: Example with n=2, p=1 on y^2=(z-a1)(z-a2)(z-a3)(z-a4). Here f = sqrt((z-a1)/(z-a2)) and f^2 = R has a pole of order 2 in the local parameter t (z = a2 + t^2) at the branch point a2; the limit (a2-a1) is nonzero.
In the same example f^2 has a zero of order 2 (n coincident zeros) at the branch point a1: the n*p = 2 zeros coincide in a group of n = 2.
A multiplier exp(2*pi*i*g) with g = 1/2 becomes 1 after raising to the n-th power with n = 2 (the common denominator), so f^n is single-valued.

transcription_corrections: Line 'bezeichnet d_μ den Werth dieser Function': 'den Werth' is an interlinear insertion above 'dieser Function'. The opening parenthesis before 'dieser' appears to be a stray mark or deletion, not a struck word.
'σ_μ, ς_μ' in the product line is written 'σ_μ, ς_μ'; the transcription is fine. The final formula reads f = ρt/(d_1 d_2 … d_p), confirmed.
